candidate_relations.reason: Reduced oxygen saturation and clubbing indicate hypoxemia, but hypoxia does not capture the multisystem TEMPI syndrome.
The IgG kappa monoclonal protein is one defining component of TEMPI syndrome, but the label omits the other syndrome features.
Polycythemia vera was the prior presumption, whereas elevated erythropoietin, hypoxemia, and the other characteristic findings support TEMPI-associated secondary erythrocytosis.
The elevated erythropoietin and hypoxemia support secondary polycythemia, but this describes only one component of TEMPI syndrome.
No obstructive lung disease is documented, and COPD does not account for the monoclonal protein, telangiectasias, and perinephric fluid collections.
A monoclonal protein alone does not establish multiple myeloma, and no myeloma-defining findings are supplied.
Telangiectasias are a defining TEMPI feature but do not represent the complete syndrome.
The record lacks the lymphadenopathy and systemic inflammatory findings expected for Castleman disease and instead presents the TEMPI feature constellation.
No VHL-associated tumors or hereditary context are described; the monoclonal protein and full constellation indicate TEMPI syndrome.
POEMS is a distinct plasma-cell syndrome requiring features such as polyneuropathy and organomegaly; the findings instead match TEMPI syndrome.
The IgG kappa monoclonal gammopathy is one component of TEMPI syndrome, without encompassing its vascular, erythropoietic, renal, and pulmonary features.
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia can cause telangiectasias and pulmonary shunting, but it does not explain the characteristic monoclonal gammopathy and perinephric fluid collections of TEMPI.
Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations can produce intrapulmonary shunting, but no discrete AVM is documented and the label omits the remaining TEMPI components.
